canonical_statement: The study aimed to generate hypotheses about differences in hyponatremia risk among individual second-generation antipsychotics using FAERS and then evaluate those associations in a large Japanese claims database.

The study used a two-stage design: disproportionality analysis in a curated FAERS-derived database for signal generation followed by a retrospective new-user cohort study in the Japanese MDV claims database for hypothesis testing.

The FAERS analysis used adverse-event case reports from 1997 Q4 through 2023 Q3 after duplicate removal, drug-name standardization, and MedDRA/J term updating by the Japan Pharmaceutical Information Center.

In the FAERS analysis, hyponatremia was defined using the narrow Standardised MedDRA Query for hyponatremia and/or syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone (SMQ 20000141), containing 15 preferred terms.

concept.text: Hyponatremia and/or syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone

outcome.definition: Narrow scope SMQ 20000141 comprising 15 preferred terms

canonical_statement: Olanzapine was the reference drug for FAERS reporting-odds-ratio comparisons because it had the largest number of hyponatremia reports, enabling stable estimates, and was widely used.

FAERS disproportionality was considered present when the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for the reporting odds ratio exceeded 1; analyses required at least 3 drug-event reports and were restricted to antipsychotic monotherapy.
The MDV claims database included data from approximately 48 million patients at 515 Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination hospitals as of April 2024.
Claims-cohort inclusion required age 18 to 69 years, at least 180 days of active medical history before the index date, and no antipsychotic use or hyponatremia during the preceding 180 days.

inclusion_criteria: At least 180 days of active medical history before index
No antipsychotic use in preceding 180 days

canonical_statement: Claims-cohort exclusions included multiple antipsychotics at index, treatment for hyponatremia in the preceding 180 days, delirium during the index hospitalization, and antineoplastic agents or chemotherapy-related supportive medications in the preceding 180 days.

population.label: MDV claims cohort exclusions
exclusion_criteria: Treatment for hyponatremia in preceding 180 days
Antineoplastic agents or chemotherapy-related supportive medications in preceding 180 days

canonical_statement: The claims primary outcome was hyponatremia defined by serum sodium below 135 mEq/L, ICD-10 E22.2 for SIADH, or ICD-10 E87.1 for hypo-osmolality and hyponatremia, during up to 180 days after antipsychotic initiation.

outcome.definition: Serum sodium <135 mEq/L, syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone (ICD-10 E22.2), or hypo-osmolality and hyponatremia (ICD-10 E87.1)

canonical_statement: Claims follow-up continued for up to 180 days and censored patients at outcome occurrence, index-drug discontinuation, death, loss to follow-up, or completion of 180 days; discontinuation used a 14-day prescription grace period.

The propensity score for each pairwise comparison with olanzapine was estimated using all measured baseline covariates, and stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to estimate the average treatment effect.

Cause-specific Cox proportional hazards models estimated crude and weighted adjusted hazard ratios; add-on use of another antipsychotic was modeled as a time-varying covariate and robust standard errors were used for 95% confidence intervals.

Claims analyses included only antipsychotics with at least 1000 patients, assessed covariate balance using an absolute standardized mean difference threshold below 0.1, and reserved weight trimming for extreme weight instability.
Prespecified secondary analyses stratified by inpatient vs outpatient treatment initiation and varied the sodium threshold and prescription grace period in sensitivity analyses.
Of 961,010 routinely prescribed antipsychotic users in the MDV database, 88,741 met inclusion criteria and 55,394 remained in the final claims cohort after exclusions.

canonical_statement: Figure 1 shows 961,010 prescribed-antipsychotic patients, 872,269 first-stage exclusions, 88,741 meeting inclusion criteria, and 33,347 subsequent exclusions; its final displayed box nevertheless repeats 88,741 rather than the 55,394 final cohort reported in the text and tables.

After weighting, propensity-score diagnostics showed mean stabilized weights of 0.995 to 1.001, 99th percentiles of 1.61 to 3.32, maximum weights of 3.84 to 19.22, and effective sample sizes of 73.4% to 94.4%; no weight trimming was applied.
Covariate balance after stabilized inverse probability weighting was generally acceptable using the prespecified absolute standardized mean difference threshold below 0.1.
Only aripiprazole had a statistically significant lower hyponatremia hazard than olanzapine in the primary weighted claims analysis.

canonical_statement: The authors interpreted the FAERS findings as hypothesis-generating and the claims findings as supporting an association between aripiprazole and lower hyponatremia risk than olanzapine in routine clinical practice.
Mechanistic explanations involving SIADH, dopamine D2 and serotonin pathways, and anticholinergic effects were presented as speculative and were not evaluated by this study.
FAERS lacks denominator data and has incomplete patient characteristics, concomitant medications, and comorbidity information, preventing incidence estimation and limiting confounding control.
Claims-based outcome definitions may misclassify hyponatremia, routine laboratory testing was incomplete, and events could be underascertained.
Claims data lacked fluid intake, psychogenic polydipsia, disease severity, and medication adherence, leaving potential confounding by indication and differential outcome ascertainment.
Prior antipsychotic exposure outside participating hospitals could not be fully ascertained, so some patients classified as incident users may have been prevalent users.
The MDV database primarily captures acute-care hospitals in Japan, limiting generalizability.
Multiple pairwise comparisons with olanzapine were performed without formal multiplicity adjustment, increasing the potential family-wise type I error rate.
Because the findings derive from observational data, causal relationships cannot be established.

The authors concluded that aripiprazole was associated with lower hyponatremia risk than olanzapine after adjustment for measured confounders, while emphasizing residual confounding, differential outcome ascertainment, and the need for further studies.
